newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open up 8.00 to 10.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open up 8.00 to 10.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 8.00 to 10.00 cents higher Thursday in a technical correction to the recent sharp sell-off, traders said.

New York arabica futures sank to six-week lows Wednesday, battered by continued speculative selling. July ended down 10.30 cents at 207.65 cents a lb after ranging between 224.00 and 206.00 cents. Active September shed 6.65 cents to 190.10 cents. The rest lost 3.80 to 6.75.
The July/September spread continued to pull back, ending at 17.55 cents against 21.20 cents Tuesday.
After Wednesday's close, CSCE said certified coffee stocks rose 828 60-kg bags as of June 10, to 44,830 bags. There were 7,500 bags pending grading.

Brazil's coffee-growing areas will see mild weather through the weekend, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp, said. Temperatures should remain in the 50s Fahrenheit, with isolated showers expected over the next several days. Soil moisture conditions should improve after last week's rains and prior to the winter dry season, WSC said.
Soil moisture is also favorable for coffee trees in West Africa, while recent rainfall has bolstered the outlook for the coffee crop in Kenya, WSC said.

In other news, the head of Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department, Mauricio Assis, said Wednesday that Brazil officially notified the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) that it has overshot its target of coffee exports in the first half of 1997.

By the end of May, Brazil coffee exports reached 6.46 million bags, with some traders also expecting sizeable shipments this month. Under an ACPC agreement, Brazil should not have shipped more than six million bags between January and June this year.

Germany's second-largest coffee roaster, Tchibo Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH, said it would raise its retail prices due to high raw coffee prices and a strong dollar. End user prices will rise to 1.40 marks per kilo, on June 26.
London robusta futures were firmer but off the highs by Thursday's midday break, with LIFFE July up $60 to $1,770.
